subsystems.name: Carbon-fixation enzyme cascade
subsystems.role: the core cycle that pulls CO2 into organic molecules without using RuBisCO.

subsystems.name: Energy and reducing-power module
subsystems.role: supplies ATP and electron carriers such as NADPH that drive the cycle.

subsystems.name: Host chassis
subsystems.role: the engineered microbe that houses and replicates the pathway.

subsystems.name: Genetic control and evolution
subsystems.role: tunes enzyme levels and selects for faster CO2 use.

subsystems.name: Product pathway
subsystems.role: routes fixed carbon into a useful chemical, fuel or biomass.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor and gas delivery
subsystems.role: feeds CO2 to the cells and removes product.

buildSteps.title: Choose a cycle
buildSteps.detail: Compare the natural Calvin cycle with synthetic alternatives (such as the CETCH cycle or the reductive glycine pathway) on paper, scoring energy cost, oxygen tolerance and enzyme count.

buildSteps.title: Source the enzymes
buildSteps.detail: Find or design carboxylases and reductases; favour variants that tolerate oxygen and moderate heat.

buildSteps.title: Reconstitute in vitro
buildSteps.detail: Mix purified enzymes and cofactors in a test tube with bicarbonate and measure CO2 fixation — the first proof that the cycle turns at all.

buildSteps.title: Improve enzyme kinetics
buildSteps.detail: Use directed evolution and rational design to lift the slowest steps, since one sluggish carboxylase can throttle the whole cycle.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the microbe
buildSteps.detail: Insert the genes as a synthetic operon into a fast-growing host, delete pathways that waste energy, and balance expression.

buildSteps.title: Couple energy supply
buildSteps.detail: Wire the cells to electricity, hydrogen, formate or light so ATP and reducing power come from outside rather than from sugar.

buildSteps.title: Evolve to grow
buildSteps.detail: Grow the strain under selection with CO2 as the main carbon source, gradually removing the sugar it used to depend on.

buildSteps.title: Scale the bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: Move from flasks to stirred tanks with efficient CO2 transfer, then test product recovery and contamination control.

buildSteps.title: Assess the whole process
buildSteps.detail: Account for the energy, the CO2 source and the end product to confirm the route is genuinely net-negative.

prerequisites.why: splitting water for hydrogen or driving electrochemistry is the usual source of energy and electrons.
capture from industry or the air gives the feedstock, though direct air capture is still costly.
multi-gene pathways must be inserted, controlled and stabilised in a living host.
natural carboxylases are slow, and synthetic ones must be made faster to be practical.
many synthetic cycles use enzymes that oxygen destroys, yet industrial microbes grow in air.

prerequisites.tech: In vitro cofactor regeneration at scale
prerequisites.why: the 2016 demonstration of a 17-enzyme synthetic cycle worked in a test tube, not a tank.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations: synthetic cycles in test tubes and bacteria that build biomass carbon from CO2 using formate or electricity
pathway.unlocks: proof that carbon fixation can beat photosynthesis per enzyme, and a toolkit of parts.

pathway.milestone: microbes that grow and divide using CO2 as their main carbon source at useful rates
pathway.unlocks: a self-replicating catalyst for making chemicals and fuels from waste gas.

pathway.milestone: pilot bioreactors running continuous gas fermentation with net-negative balance
pathway.unlocks: drop-in chemicals, proteins or fuels with a verified carbon footprint.

pathway.milestone: industrial plants linked to CO2 capture, running at costs competitive with fossil feedstocks
pathway.unlocks: large-scale recycling of carbon dioxide into materials rather than storing it underground.
